mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 falls by more than 2% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly unemployment rate below 5% for four consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE remains below 5% for four consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual tightening of monetary policy and rising inflation, which increases real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month moving averages simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent decline in both real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS) and housing starts (HOUST) for three consecutive months signals a broad-based weakening in demand drivers, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and HOUST both decline for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both PAYEMS and HOUST decline for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.4 percentage points in a single month signals a sharp deterioration in labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profitability, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls by >0.4pp in one month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE drops by more than 0.4 percentage points in a month.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent year-over-year increase in real personal savings (proxied by RSAFS) above 10% for four consecutive months signals elevated precautionary savings and reduced consumer spending, which depresses demand and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days, except during periods of fiscal stimulus.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS YoY growth > 10% for 4 consecutive months and no fiscal stimulus announced
regime_hint: precautionary savings regime without fiscal stimulus
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when RSAFS YoY growth exceeds 10% for four months and no fiscal stimulus is announced.
